plan: Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value of $9 is the dominant strategy. This means I should bid $9.0 to maximize my expected profit. By bidding my true value, I ensure I only win when the prize is worth more to me than the second-highest bid. This strategy minimizes the risk of overpaying and provides the most rational approach given the single-round nature of this auction.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $40. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item when I value it highly
2. Bidding more than my value could result in a loss if I win
3. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, truthful bidding minimizes potential regret
4. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes honest valuation
So I will bid exactly my private value.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my true value ($32) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. By bidding my true value, I maximize potential profit - I'll win if my value is highest, and pay only the second-highest bid. Since values are independently and randomly drawn, strategic deviations are unlikely to improve my expected outcome. I'll follow the rational, theoretically optimal approach.
